newsitem.title: UK: FOCUS-Pound zooms to 2-1/2 yr high on rate rise.
newsitem.headline: FOCUS-Pound zooms to 2-1/2 yr high on rate rise.

text.p: Sterling surged to a 2-1/2 year high on a trade-weighted basis after the Bank of England surprised markets on Wednesday by raising British interest rates by a quarter-point to 6.0 percent.
The pound also set a 19-month peak against the dollar at $1.6340 and rose to a 22-month high at 2.4640 marks.
Analysts said sterling was likely to accelerate further since the rate rise has added to Chancellor of the Exchequer Kenneth Clarke's credibility as finance minister.

"It's good news for the pound," said Paul Meggyesi, senior currency economist at Deutsche Morgan Grenfell. "By moving so early, Clarke has reduced the risk his credibility will be called into question, which was a potential pound-negative."
The rate rise sent a strong signal to the market that the government is not opposed to the pound firming further, he said.

The pound has risen almost seven percent on a trade-weighted basis since the beginning of August. The trade-weighted index was at 90.3 at 1326 GMT, its highest level since March 1994, and up 1.4 percent from Tuesday's close at 89.1.
The pound was at 2.4620 marks, just off a 22-month peak, and up from from 2.4496 marks before the tightening.
Cable was at $1.6312, just off a post-rate rise 19-month high at $1.6340 and up from $1.6203 before the announcement.
Jeremy Hawkins, chief economist Europe at BankAmerica here, said the move was positive for the pound because it boosted the credibility of the government's anti-inflation policy.
"To this end, the news should be medium-term positive for gilts and certainly supportive of sterling," said Hawkins.

Clarke said the rise reduced the risk for larger increases later and improved the chances of hitting the underlying inflation target of 2.5 percent. Underlying inflation, excluding mortgage interest payments, stood at 2.9 percent in September.
Bank of England governor Eddie George said the rate rise was due to the moderate accelerating pace of the economic upswing.

Analysts said sterling could now easily move to 2.50 marks before the election. Clarke's decision to raise rates ahead of the general election, due by May 1997, showed that he might be prepared to tighten credit again before the poll, they said.
"This has simply got to be good news for sterling, with both yield differentials and the domestic consumption now moving in its favour," said Peter von Maydell, senior economist at UBS.
Sterling's rally over the past months has been fuelled by its relative yield attractions, rising oil prices and an improving current account balance.
The pound had already had a strong run ahead of the rate rise, led by heavy demand for cable. The People's Bank of China was said to have bought cable quite aggressively, traders said.

There was also talk of sterling buying linked to Dieter Bock's sale of his stake in Lonrho to South African mining giant Anglo American. The talk was based on the theory that rand would be swapped for dollars, then for sterling.
